::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** [19 ?October or November 1861]  
**Manuscript:** MS location unknown. Printed in Yonge, <i>[Life of John Coleridge Patteson](cmy_books/cmybook_102.qmd)</i> I, 550
:::

How can [I](people/person_1155.qmd) grieve and sorrow about my dear dear [Father](people/person_1156.qmd)’s blessed end? . . . I shall like the photograph of Hursley Vicarage and Church, the lawn and group upon it.[^1] But most shall I like to think that [Mr. Keble](people/person_798.qmd), and I dare say [Dr. Moberly](people/person_1015.qmd) too, pray for me and this [Mission](organizations/other_30.qmd). I need the prayers of all good people indeed.

---

[^1]: CMY introduces the letter by saying it 'contained thanks for a photograph of Hursley Church spire and Vicarage, which had been taken one summer afternoon, at the desire of Dr. Moberly (the present Bishop of Salisbury), and of which I had begged a copy for him'.  The photograph is probably that reproduced in *Dulce Domum facing page 184.  It shows Moberly and Keble standing, with CMY and Charlotte Keble seated, in the garden of Hursley Vicarage.
